Plausibility band for a binormal net-benefit curve from PR-AUC uncertainty

Source: R/fn_net_benefit.R
nb_binormal_band.Rd

The summary route (nb_binormal) anchors an entire decision curve to a single reported PR-AUC, almost always a point estimate with no stated uncertainty. This propagates a plausible spread in that PR-AUC into a band on the net-benefit curve, extending ap_scalar_to_prev from a point reconstruction to an interval one.

Usage

nb_binormal_band(
  pr_auc,
  pi,
  pt,
  spread,
  side = c("lower", "both"),
  pi0 = pi,
  grid = 3000
)

Arguments

pr_auc

Reported PR-AUC (average precision) at the evaluation prevalence, a single value.

pi

Target landscape prevalence in (0, 1).

pt

Numeric vector of threshold probabilities.

spread

Half-width of the plausible PR-AUC range, in PR-AUC units (e.g. 0.04 for +/- 0.04). Calibrate from replicate-model spread.

side

"lower" (default) for a one-sided lower band, or "both" for lower and upper edges.

pi0

Evaluation prevalence the PR-AUC was measured at. Defaults to pi.

grid

Integration grid passed to ap_binormal when inverting the PR-AUC.

Value

A data frame with one row per pt: pt, the central curve nb, and lower (plus upper when side = "both"). The fitted separations are attached as attribute "mu" (named central, lower, and upper when two-sided).

Details

The perturbation is anchored on the PR-AUC scale, not on mu directly: a fixed shift in mu has no stable meaning across taxa or prevalences, whereas a spread in PR-AUC is what replicate train/test partitions actually show. The reported PR-AUC and its spread-perturbed endpoints are each converted to a binormal separation by inverting ap_binormal at the evaluation prevalence pi0, then read off nb_binormal at the target prevalence. Because nb_binormal is monotone increasing in mu, the PR-AUC endpoints map straight to the band edges.

This is a plausibility band (a sensitivity analysis over an assumed PR-AUC spread), not a confidence interval: with only a reported scalar there is no sampling distribution. Calibrate spread from replicate models when you have them; see nb_exact_ci for the model-free sampling band when raw predictions are available.

Only a lower band is returned by default, matching nb_exact_ci: in decision-curve analysis the decision-relevant uncertainty is the downside – whether the model could be worse than a default strategy. Use side = "both" for upper and lower edges.
